context_label: Metastatic ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer
title: Five-day topotecan for ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer
schedule_label: A 30-minute infusion on each of five consecutive days, then a break through day 21. The standard plan is up to six cycles, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity.
schedule_summary: A 30-minute infusion on each of five consecutive days, then a break through day 21. The standard plan is up to six cycles, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity.
purpose: Topotecan is being offered to slow the growth of metastatic ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer. Your team will review symptoms and scan results with you to decide whether to continue.
indication_text: Metastatic ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal carcinoma after earlier treatment has failed. The fallopian tube and peritoneal indications are unlicensed in Ireland.
administration_text: You attend the unit for each prescribed daily infusion. A consultant may shorten a course to three or four days for toxicity or after extensive previous treatment. Follow your written calendar.
monitoring_summary: Blood count and kidney and liver tests before starting. Kidney function helps determine the starting dose. Repeat blood count and kidney and liver tests before each cycle. Low neutrophils, platelets or haemoglobin may require delay, dose change or supportive treatment. Symptoms and imaging according to your consultant’s plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Topotecan
agents.explanation: Topotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves strain while DNA is copied. Unrepaired DNA breaks can stop dividing cancer cells; healthy blood-forming and gut cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Call oncology immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, severe tummy pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or new cough or breathlessness. Do not wait for the next cycle.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and mouth soreness
Rare severe bowel inflammation or perforation
consent_risks: Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness. Low platelets can cause bruising, nosebleeds or bleeding gums.
Nausea, diarrhoea and mouth ulcers can make drinking difficult. Call if you cannot keep fluids down.
Low neutrophils can lead to sepsis. Fever, chills or sudden illness require an urgent call.
Tell the team about unexpected bruising or bleeding. Seek urgent help if bleeding continues.
Fever with abdominal pain or diarrhoea needs urgent review. Report new or worsening cough or breathlessness.

Tell the team about ulcers or painful swallowing; ask for help if you cannot drink.
New cough, breathlessness or chest pain needs urgent assessment.

questions.q: What should I check before treatment?
questions.a: Confirm all five visit dates and bring your anti-sickness medicines list. Tell your team about previous low blood counts, infection or kidney problems.

questions.q: What should I watch for at home?
questions.a: Keep taking fluids if able. Record diarrhoea, mouth soreness, bruising or breathlessness. Ring urgently for fever with abdominal pain or diarrhoea.

evidence.title: Randomised ovarian cancer trial of PLD versus topotecan
evidence.interpretation: Among 474 participants with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer, tumour response occurred in 19.7% with PLD and 17.0% with topotecan.
evidence.limitations: The response-rate difference was not statistically significant. Results from ovarian cancer cannot give a separate response estimate for fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer.

prescription_phases.label: Day 1 · Topotecan

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.timing: Up to three times daily if needed; at least 6 hours apart. Maximum 30 mg or 0.5 mg/kg per day, whichever is lower, for up to 5 days.

additional_support: Confirm all five visit dates and bring your anti-sickness medicines list. Tell your team about previous low blood counts, infection or kidney problems.
prescription_phases.guidance: Use on this treatment day only. Check doses already taken. One rescue supply for the cycle; do not restart a five-day rescue course at each visit.
prescription_phases.prescription_source: NCCP 00311 and NCIS medical oncology antiemetics
prescription_notes: Use on this treatment day only. Check doses already taken. One rescue supply for the cycle; do not restart a five-day rescue course at each visit.

local_adjuncts.directions: Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
Rinse 10 mL around the mouth for at least 1 minute four times daily; expel after rinsing.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take 4 mg after the first episode of diarrhoea, then 2 mg after each further episode, to a maximum of 16 mg/day.
